newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Greens MP defects to Kohl's CDU.
newsitem.headline: German Greens MP defects to Kohl's CDU.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) notched up an unusual political success on Monday when a member of parliament for the leftist-environmentalist Greens defected to the CDU.

Vera Lengsfeld, one of a number of former East German civil rights activists whom Kohl's party have been courting for the last two years, said she could no longer tolerate the Greens cosying up to the Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS), successors to East Berlin's communist rulers.
"Out of pure power politics, the Greens are in the process of throwing overboard most of what the East German opposition stood for," she wrote in a letter to the Greens party leadership.
"I can't work for a party which is latently becoming more and more prepared to help the PDS back to power in order to get into power itself."

After German unification, the Greens drew most of their membership in east Germany from the Alliance 90 civil rights movement rather than environmentalists or leftists, and they formally renamed themselves Alliance 90/Greens.

But the Greens are weak in eastern Germany, where the strength of the PDS means it often holds the balance of power between Kohl's CDU and possible regional coalitions of centre-left Social Democrats and Greens.
Lengsfeld said the Greens were now betraying the East German civil rights movement by consorting with the communists they once fought.

Lengsfeld herself was a famous victim of the communist security apparatus under her married name Wollenberger. She found out in 1992 that her own husband Knud had for years spied on her for the ministry of state security. She divorced him and took back her maiden name.
She told the daily Thueringer Allgemeine that Kohl's CDU not only determinedly rejected cooperation with the PDS but was also now "the only party trying to reform society".
Her defection raised the theoretical majority of Kohl's centre-right government to 12 from 10.
Although she announced her intention to remain in parliament, the Greens leadership urged her to "follow her own sense of democracy" and resign her seat.
